opportunities.title: The Ledger 'Spy Chip' Wasn't a Software Bug — It Was a Supply Chain, and CryptoBilis Was the Vector
opportunities.why_now: Ledger confirmed losses may exceed $86M from hardware implants that transmit recovery phrases over LTE, traced to a single reseller — a textbook supply-chain compromise unfolding in real time.
opportunities.angle: Explainer/breakdown: how the implant worked, why 'buy from the source' was always the real rule, and a checklist for verifying hardware wallet provenance before you trust a seed phrase to it.

opportunities.title: Coldcard's X Account Got Phished — If It Can Happen to a Security Vendor, Your DMs Are Not Safe
opportunities.why_now: A phishing link appeared on Coldcard's own official X account mid-Ledger-crisis, showing even security-focused brands aren't immune to account takeover.
opportunities.angle: Hot take/thread: the irony of a hardware security company's social account getting hijacked during the industry's worst week — reminder that 'official account' is not a trust signal, link hygiene is non-negotiable.

opportunities.title: UK Just Told You Seized Bitcoin Isn't Yours Even If a Court Took It From a Scammer
opportunities.why_now: A High Court ruling strengthens the UK government's claim to keep $5B in seized BTC, setting precedent for how states treat confiscated crypto as a sovereign asset, not victim restitution.
opportunities.angle: Analysis: what this precedent means for anyone relying on 'the state will return it' as a backstop, and how custody risk extends beyond hacks into legal seizure.

opportunities.title: France Wants Your Wallet Reported at $112K — Here's Why That Number Was Never the Point
opportunities.why_now: A French proposal to mandate reporting of wallets over $112K is drawing immediate 'leave' backlash from the crypto community, reviving the surveillance-vs-self-custody fight.
opportunities.angle: Opinion piece: why arbitrary reporting thresholds always ratchet down over time, framed as 'you already know how this ends' — use Ledger breach week as proof custodial trust (in hardware or regulators) keeps failing.

opportunities.title: THEO Down 92% After Base Bridge Exploit — Another Week, Another Bridge That Wasn't Ready
opportunities.why_now: Autheo's THEO token collapsed 92% following a suspected bridge exploit on Base, adding to 2026's running tally of cross-chain bridge failures.
opportunities.angle: Quick-hit incident post: what's known so far, how the exploit likely worked, and a standing reminder that bridges remain the single riskiest primitive in DeFi — pair with a running 'bridge body count' graphic.
